objective.statement: Learn the scales and key signatures of E major and A flat major.
successCriteria: I know E major has four sharps: F, C, G and D.
I know A flat major has four flats: B, E, A and D.
I can write both scales and both key signatures.

explanation.text: Grade 3 takes key signatures up to four sharps or four flats. Two new major keys arrive: E major, with four sharps, and A flat major, with four flats.

music.textAlternative: The scale of E major in the treble clef with its key signature of four sharps: E, F sharp, G sharp, A, B, C sharp, D sharp, E.

explanation.caption: E major: four sharps (F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯), the new one being D♯.

music.textAlternative: The scale of A flat major in the treble clef with its key signature of four flats: A flat, B flat, C, D flat, E flat, F, G, A flat.

explanation.caption: A♭ major: four flats (B♭ E♭ A♭ D♭), the new one being D♭.

explanation.text: Sharps are added in the order F, C, G, D, A, E, B. Flats are added in the order B, E, A, D, G, C, F. Four sharps use the first four letters of the sharp order, and four flats use the first four of the flat order.

Two quick checks for MAJOR keys. In a sharp major key, the key note is a semitone above the last sharp: the last sharp of E major is D sharp, and E is a semitone above it. In a flat major key with two or more flats, the major key is named by the second-last flat: in A flat major the flats are B, E, A, D, and the second-last is A. Every key signature also belongs to a relative minor, so check which one the music is in. Written without a key signature, a scale needs its accidentals beside the notes. E major has sharps on F, G, C and D. A flat major has flats on B, E, A and D. Coming down, the same accidentals are used.
E major: F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯. A♭ major: B♭ E♭ A♭ D♭. The major scale pattern is tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone.

music.textAlternative: A flat major scale: A flat, B flat, C, D flat, E flat, F, G, A flat.
